title: How the Python SDK edits the security allowlist and denylist

prose.text: This covers how the Python SDK edits the global allowlist and denylist URL lists. It is a statement about the client; what the service stores is on the product side.

checks.do: Which helper changed the list, since allowlist helpers rewrite the whole list and denylist helpers send one action.
Whether another admin or script changed the allowlist around the same time as a helper call.

allowlist-add-delete-replace-whole-list.statement: `add_urls_to_whitelist` and `delete_urls_from_whitelist` read the current allowlist, change it in the client, and write the whole list back through `replace_whitelist`, which sends a PUT to `/security` with `whitelistUrls`.

quotes: whitelist.whitelist_urls.extend(url for url in url_list if url not in whitelist.whitelist_urls)
whitelist.whitelist_urls = [url for url in whitelist.whitelist_urls if url not in url_list]

allowlist-write-not-atomic.statement: Two allowlist changes made between one helper's read and its write can overwrite each other, since the write replaces the whole list.
allowlist-write-not-atomic.conditions: Holds when another change to the allowlist lands between the helper's read and its PUT; the helper code takes no lock and sends no version or precondition.

denylist-add-delete-action-endpoint.statement: `add_urls_to_blacklist` and `delete_urls_from_blacklist` send a POST to `/security/advanced/blacklistUrls` with query parameter `action` set to ADD_TO_LIST or REMOVE_FROM_LIST and body `blacklistUrls`; they do not read and rewrite the list.

quotes: http_method = "post".upper() api_url = format_url(f"{self._zia_base_endpoint}/security/advanced/blacklistUrls") params = {"action": "ADD_TO_LIST"} payload = {"blacklistUrls": url_list} request, error = self._request_executor.create_request(http_method, api_url, payload, params=params)

http_method = "post".upper() api_url = format_url(f"{self._zia_base_endpoint}/security/advanced/blacklistUrls") params = {"action": "REMOVE_FROM_LIST"} payload = {"blacklistUrls": url_list} request, error = self._request_executor.create_request(http_method, api_url, payload, params=params)

denylist-replace-and-erase.statement: `replace_blacklist` sends a PUT to `/security/advanced` with `blacklistUrls`, and `erase_blacklist` and `erase_whitelist` are the replace calls with an empty list.
